recipes.name: Oatmeal with Berries & Flax Seeds
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in soluble fiber from oats which can help lower LDL cholesterol, and provides Omega-3 fatty acids from flax seeds which contribute to heart health. Fortified milk adds Vitamin D.

ingredients.item: Optional: dash of cinnamon or maple syrup

instructions: Combine oats and milk in a saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally, until oats are cooked and liquid is absorbed (about 5-7 minutes).
Pour into a bowl and top with mixed berries, ground flax seeds, and slivered almonds.
Add cinnamon or a touch of maple syrup if desired.

recipes.name: Lentil (Dal Tadka) & Mixed Vegetable Curry
recipes.health_benefit: Packed with soluble fiber from lentils and vegetables, this dish can actively help reduce LDL cholesterol. Lentils are also an excellent source of plant-based protein.

ingredients.item: Mixed vegetables (carrots, peas, spinach, bell peppers)

instructions: Wash and soak toor dal for 20 minutes. Drain.
In a pressure cooker or pot, combine dal, mixed vegetables, turmeric, and 3 cups of water. Cook until dal is tender.
In a separate pan, heat olive oil. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Once spluttering, add chopped onion and sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for 1 minute. Add chopped tomato, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook until tomatoes soften.
Add the cooked dal and vegetables to the tempering. Add more water if needed to adjust consistency. Season with salt and garam masala.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander.

recipes.name: Spinach and Mushroom Quinoa Pulao
recipes.health_benefit: Quinoa offers complete plant protein and fiber, helping with satiety and cholesterol management. Mushrooms, especially if sun-exposed or UV-treated, contribute to Vitamin D intake, while spinach provides essential micronutrients.
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water.
Heat olive oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their water and brown lightly.
Stir in turmeric powder. Add quinoa, water/broth, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed.
Stir in fresh spinach and cook until wilted. Fluff with a fork.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

recipes.name: Tofu Scramble with Turmeric and Veggies
recipes.health_benefit: A plant-based, egg-free alternative that provides lean protein and fiber without contributing to LDL cholesterol. Turmeric adds anti-inflammatory benefits, and the vegetables enhance nutrient density.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add chopped onion and bell pepper, sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add crumbled tofu to the pan. Break it up further with your spatula.
Stir in nutritional yeast, turmeric powder, garlic powder, black salt (if using), salt, and pepper. Mix well to coat the tofu.
Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tofu is heated through and slightly browned.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Serve hot, perhaps with whole wheat toast.

recipes.name: Chickpea & Vegetable Curry
recipes.health_benefit: This fiber-rich, plant-based curry provides significant soluble fiber from chickpeas, which is crucial for lowering LDL cholesterol. It's also a great source of lean protein.

ingredients.item: Mixed vegetables (e.g., cauliflower, green beans, potatoes)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili (if using), cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and curry powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add pureed tomatoes and cook until the oil starts to separate, about 5-7 minutes.
Add chopped mixed vegetables and chickpeas. Pour in water or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally. Season with salt.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Chia Seed Pudding with Fortified Soy Milk and Fruits
recipes.health_benefit: Chia seeds are a rich source of soluble fiber and Omega-3 fatty acids (ALA), both beneficial for managing LDL cholesterol. Fortified soy milk significantly contributes to Vitamin D intake, addressing the patient's low levels.

ingredients.item: Fortified soy milk (or other fortified plant milk)
Mixed berries or sliced fruit (e.g., banana, mango)

instructions: In a jar or bowl, combine chia seeds, fortified soy milk, maple syrup/honey (if using), and vanilla extract.
Stir well to ensure there are no clumps of chia seeds.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until the mixture has thickened to a pudding-like consistency.
Before serving, stir again and top with fresh mixed berries or sliced fruit.

recipes.name: Mixed Bean Chili
recipes.health_benefit: This chili is a powerhouse of dietary fiber from multiple bean types, which is excellent for lowering LDL cholesterol. It also provides substantial plant-based protein and is naturally low in saturated fat.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion and bell peppers; sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in chili powder, cumin powder, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes (undrained), kidney beans, black beans, chickpeas, and vegetable broth. Stir well.
Bring the chili to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and let it cook for at least 20-30 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Stir occasionally.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh coriander or parsley. Can be served with a small side of whole-grain bread or a dollop of low-fat yogurt.
